title: PYSEC-2025-19
summary: Affected: PyPI: picklescan picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

title: PYSEC-2024-115
summary: Affected: PyPI: langchain-community A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

title: CVE-2026-116158 — ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 Memory Leak in magick compare
summary: Affected: ImageMagick ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 contains a memory leak vulnerability in the magick compare command caused by missing cleanup when an operation fails. Attackers can supply inputs that trigger repeated failed compare operations to exhaust memory and cause denial of service.

title: CVE-2026-96187 — Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Information Disclosure Vulnerability
summary: Affected: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

title: CVE-2026-88078 — Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Spoofing Vulnerability
summary: Affected: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Improper verification of cryptographic signature in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

title: CVE-2026-120754 — Uninitialized Heap Memory Disclosure via Truncated Chunk in HDF5 Scale-Offset Filter
summary: Affected: The HDF Group Scale-Offset Filter HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains an uninitialized memory read vulnerability in H5Z__filter_scaleoffset() in src/H5Zscaleoffset.c. The decode path validates reads against the allocated size of the chunk buffer rather than the number of bytes actually read from the file. Because H5D__chunk_lock() deliberately sizes filtered chunk buffers to the larger of the stored and unfiltered chunk sizes and fills only the stored bytes, a truncated chunk passes these bounds checks and is decompressed from the uninitialized remainder of the allocation. Unrelated heap contents are then returned to the caller as dataset data. Because the reads remain within the allocation, the issue is not detected by AddressSanitizer. An attacker who can get a user or application to read a dataset from a crafted HDF5 file can cause disclosure of process memory. This issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-19029.

title: CVE-2026-112593
summary: Affected: Apple macOS An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking. This issue is fixed in macOS Sequoia 15.8.2, macOS Tahoe 26.7.2. An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or write kernel memory.

title: CVE-2026-20942 — Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Spoofing Vulnerability
summary: Affected: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Improper restriction of rendered ui layers or frames in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

title: CVE-2026-85890 — Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
summary: Affected: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Double free in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

title: CVE-2026-121564 — Silent loss of messages when merging overlapping chat exports in whatstk
summary: Affected: lucasrodes whatstk Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors (CWE-1023) in merge_chats() (whatstk/utils/chat_merge.py), reached from BaseChat.merge(), in whatstk from 0.3.0 before 0.9.0 allows a party that supplies the chat exports to cause messages to be absent from the merged output with no indication that anything was removed, because the merge keeps whole the chat whose first message is oldest and appends from the other only the messages that are strictly newer than the last message of the first. Every message of the second chat that falls inside the date range already covered by the first is therefore discarded. The two chats are compared on their date ranges and not on the identity of the individual messages, so a message held by only one of the two exports is dropped whenever its date falls inside the range of the other, and both branches of _merge_two_chats() behave this way. The merged result is returned without a warning and without a count of what was removed. This results in a merged chat that omits messages the inputs contain, in a library whose documented uses include forensic review and the generation of training data.
